# Platform.Storage.Cache.read()

Reads a temporary cache file.

## Syntax

<CodeBlock language="ts">
  <span style={{ display: 'inline' }}>SpotifyPlus.Platform.Storage.Cache.read&lt;T = any&gt;(path: string): T | string | Uint8Array | null</span>
</CodeBlock>

## Examples

The following example shows how an extension can use a recent cached search if Android has kept it.

```ts
// Use a recent cached search if Android has kept it.
type CachedSearch = { query: string; items: Array<{ uri: string; text: string }> };
const cached = SpotifyPlus.Platform.Storage.Cache.read<CachedSearch>('search/after-hours.json');

if (cached && typeof cached !== 'string' && !(cached instanceof Uint8Array)) {
  console.log(`Cached results for ${cached.query}:`, cached.items.length);
} else {
  console.log('Cache was cleared. Please run Search.search() again');
}
```

## Parameters

`path`

<Badge>string</Badge> <Badge variant="danger">Required</Badge>

A path relative to this extension’s storage area.

## Returns

`T | string | Uint8Array | null`

The stored value, or null if missing. Although Android will almost never clear the cache itself, so not very likely unless if the user cleared it themself.


Reads local extension storage synchronously. Returns the decoded value directly, or `null` when no value is available.
